about: The sourced production rules (docs/SOURCED_RULES.md). Source types: A article/official page/study, B book, C YouTube video or vlog. binding = two or more types and enforced in code; hypothesis = one type, REVIEW only, the project's existing number; house = the creator's dated decision.

rules.statement: Heard pace is measured on the finished read: words divided by the read's duration, pauses included; target 170 wpm, accepted 155-185; one band everywhere (five studies agree 170 is the YouTube norm; one source type, so the project's own number stays). Every estimate uses this one definition: a Short's length and ST-13's turn cadence are its words at the target; the long video's estimated read times each word at the script's voice.pace_wpm (the voice's speaking rate) and adds the punctuation and held pauses, and PV-52 compares the heard pace of that estimate (words / estimated duration) with the band.

rules.statement: No pause before a punch line (performers do not pause there); emphasis comes from the text (one stressed word, an ellipsis, a tag), never from a hold over one second. The hold limit governs the narrator's pauses (a narration line's pause_after); a scripted silence inside a dialogue scene is a scene device, not a narration hold. Exempt: the last narration line of a segment before a change of place or time (BP-31's scene boundary) may hold a breath up to boundary_breath_max_s; longer is a REVIEW (NR-07: naming the jump is sourced, the seconds are a hypothesis).

rules.statement: Cut continuity: across a hard cut the hero or focal point stays within 10 % of the frame of its previous position unless the cut opens a new scene; the shot size changes by a full step (never the same framing of the same picture twice in a row); a direction change over 90 degrees needs a neutral picture between.
